title: Is the Nile or the Amazon the longest river?
examples: Which is the longest river in the world?
Is the Amazon longer than the Nile?

explain.say: Imagine a race between two giant rivers. One runs through the hot desert of Africa, the other through the green rainforest of South America. Which one is longer? Look at the two rivers on the board.

draw.text: Is the Nile or the Amazon the longest river?

explain.say: Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: a river from source to sea. Look at the source, the upper course and the tributary. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

draw.text: Is the Nile or the Amazon the longest river?

explain.say: On the left is the Nile. Most maps say it is about 6,650 kilometres long, flowing north through 11 countries, like Uganda, Sudan and Egypt, into the Mediterranean Sea. Can you find its length?
On the right is the Amazon, about 6,400 kilometres on most maps. But look at the third point: it carries far more water than any other river, about one fifth of all river water reaching the oceans.

So why do people argue? A river's start, called its source, is often a tiny stream high in the hills, and it is hard to say which stream counts. Some scientists measured the Amazon as longer! Which river would you pick?
Good thinking! Look at the verdict: the Nile usually wins on length, the Amazon on size. Wow fact: no bridge crosses the main Amazon river anywhere along its whole length.

faq.a: About 6,650 kilometres, from streams that feed Lake Victoria in East Africa to the Mediterranean Sea in Egypt. Most atlases call it the longest river.
asks: What is the length of the Nile?

faq.q: Is the Amazon longer than the Nile?
faq.a: Most maps say no: the Amazon is about 6,400 kilometres. But some scientists who chose a farther source in Peru measured it as longer, so the race is still argued about.
asks: Which is longer, Nile or Amazon?

faq.q: What is the source of a river?
faq.a: The source is where a river begins, often a spring, a lake or melting snow high in the hills. Tiny streams join to make the river bigger.

faq.q: Why does the Amazon carry so much water?
faq.a: It drains a huge rainy area of South America, with more than a thousand rivers joining it. Heavy rainforest rain keeps it full all year.
asks: Which river has the most water?

faq.q: Why is there no bridge over the Amazon?
faq.a: Much of it flows through thick rainforest with few roads, and the river is very wide and floods each year, so boats are used instead.
asks: Are there bridges over the Amazon?

facts: The Nile is usually measured at about 6,650 kilometres and the Amazon at about 6,400 kilometres.
The Amazon carries about one fifth of all the river water that flows into the world's oceans.

quiz.say: Which river carries the most water in the world?
quiz.show: Which river carries the most water in the world?
quiz.why: The Amazon carries far more water than any other river.

wrong.0: The Nile is long, but it flows through dry desert and carries much less water.
wrong.2: The Thames in England is short, about 346 kilometres.

quiz.say: Why do people disagree about the longest river?
quiz.show: Why do people disagree about the longest river?

options.show: It is hard to agree where a river's source is
options.say: It is hard to agree where a river's source is

quiz.why: A river begins as many tiny streams, so people choose different sources and get different lengths.

wrong.1: Rivers change only slowly, over many years.
wrong.2: Both rivers have been measured many times, with satellites too.
